issue.title: delegate.md still says a fan-out cannot be reached from an operator's sentence
issue.body:
\`docs/coder/delegate.md\`, section "What is not built", lists:

> **Reaching a fan-out from an operator's sentence.** \`coder::runtime\` runs the program, and the program still runs from a caller in Rust.

That landed: \`coder::turn::run\` asks \`openagents.program.v1\` before it classifies, a program answer runs \`Runtime::run\`, and the CoderBench golden \`devin-fan-out-six\` is recorded from \`coder -p\` on Linux (\`docs/programs.md\`, "How a sentence reaches it"). The page also does not mention that a \`delegate\` step's \`isolation: worktree\` and \`writes: true\` retain a worktree under \`.coder/worktrees\` for a reviewer, which is how the \`burn-down\` program hands work back.

## What to do

- Remove or rewrite the stale bullet so the page states how the runtime is reached today, linking \`docs/programs.md\` rather than repeating it.
- Under "Isolation is provided or refused, never pretended", say in one or two sentences what a reviewer does with a retained worktree (\`git worktree list\`, inspect, merge or remove) — the program runs it, the operator finishes it.
- Google developer documentation style (\`.agents/skills/google-developer-style/SKILL.md\`). Change only \`docs/coder/delegate.md\`.

## Acceptance

- The "What is not built" section names only things that are not built.
- A reader knows where a writing delegate's edits end up and what to do with them.
